events.text: CPF's 2024 Sustainability Report reports a 27% reduction in direct and indirect GHG emissions per production unit in Thailand against a 2015 base year.
CPF's 2024 Sustainability Report reports that 56% of revenue came from green products.
CPF's 2025 Sustainability Report states the company became the first food producer with SBTi-validated near-term and long-term net-zero targets for 2050.
CPF's 2025 Sustainability Report states the company achieved 100% coal-free operations across nine countries.

In 2025, the Company conducted a sustainability materiality assessment across its agro-industrial and food value chain, reviewing key internal and external factors including major economic, social, and environmental risks.
Key achievements in 2025 include becoming the first food producer with SBTi-validated near-term and long-term net-zero targets for 2050.
Key achievements in 2025 include achieving 100% coal-free operations across nine countries.
A Thai court accepted a class action lawsuit against Charoen Pokphand Foods for causing environmental damage from the rapid spread of an invasive fish species.

The first hearing was held in a defamation lawsuit brought in Thailand by Charoen Pokphand Foods (CPF) against an environmental group that allegedly suggested the seafood giant introduced blackchin tilapia.
Witoon Lianchamroon, secretary-general of the BIOTHAI Foundation, appeared in court on October 22 to face charges filed by Charoen Pokphand Foods (CPF).
